prompt:
A sharp close-up photograph, camera level with the base, of a four-post acrylic stacking puzzle in a bright studio: a flat base with FOUR upright pegs standing on it, marked A, B, C and D from left to right.

It carries 6 round disks of clearly different widths -- disk 1 (the narrowest) is pink, disk 2 is yellow, disk 3 is sky blue, disk 4 is lime, disk 5 is lavender, disk 6 is peach (the widest) -- each with its own size number printed large on its face. The stacking rule is the usual one -- a disk rests either on the base or on a disk wider than itself, never on a narrower one.

At the start the disks lie like this:
    - peg A holds, from the BOTTOM upward: disk 2, then disk 1
    - peg B holds, from the BOTTOM upward: disk 6, then disk 5, then disk 4, then disk 3
    - peg C is EMPTY
    - peg D is EMPTY

Someone now gathers all 6 disks onto peg D in the FEWEST possible moves, and ALL FOUR pegs may be used as resting places. The shortest way needs exactly 16 moves -- one disk at a time, always the top disk of a peg, never a wider disk onto a narrower one. Every shortest solution stands in the SAME arrangement after move 9.

Show the puzzle EXACTLY as it stands at that instant, immediately after move 9. Every disk must sit on the peg it really occupies then, in the correct order; a peg holding no disk must be drawn empty.

Keep the picture clean: no move list, no annotations, no captions. The only characters in the image are the letters on the base and the number printed on each disk.
